label: the borrowed consonants z, f and q as sounds, not just as spellings
note: The spoken twin of HI-A1-SCR-16, closed the way PH-01 through PH-04 were: on a script atom that teaches the contrast rather than a separate pronunciation lesson. HI-S141-nuqta-borrowed names z, f, x and q as sounds, places the last two further back in the mouth than their plain letters, and says plainly that many speakers merge them. It builds on HI-C37-khaana, which had already named the nuqta for ONE pair -- khaanaa food against khaanaa a compartment -- as a fact about those two words, and told the truth that the dot is often left off in print.
